lens: The sexually dimorphic response to caloric restriction in intestinal tumorigenesis challenges universal dietary interventions, revealing that CR's anti-cancer efficacy is mechanistically tied to sex-specific pathways, necessitating a shift toward personalized, sex-stratified nutritional strategies.
known_to_ignore: Caloric restriction reduces body weight and improves insulin sensitivity
Dietary restriction extends lifespan in model organisms
CR lowers inflammatory markers like hs-CRP and IL-6
tensions: CR reduces macroadenomas in male Apc(1638N/+) mice but not in females, while visceral fat removal is effective only in females (facts 31457 vs 31458)
Metabolic reductions in leptin and IGF-1 under CR are observed in male mice (facts 3312, 3313), but their direct role in sex-specific cancer outcomes remains unlinked
gaps: The effect of CR on intestinal tumorigenesis in female mice beyond the Apc(1638N/+) model is undercharacterized
Dose- and timing-dependent effects of CR on sex-specific cancer outcomes are not defined
Integration of metabolic (e.g., leptin, IGF-1) and inflammatory markers in sex-stratified CR studies is lacking

theses.title: Sex-Stratified Efficacy of Caloric Restriction in Intestinal Cancer: Evidence from Genetic Mouse Models
theses.rationale: Direct evidence from Apc(1638N/+) mice shows clear sex differences in CR's ability to reduce macroadenomas, highlighting a critical gap in personalized dietary cancer prevention research that could inform targeted interventions.

theses.title: Comparative Analysis of Caloric Restriction and Rapamycin on Proteome Stability in Aging Cardiac Tissue
theses.rationale: Short-term CR enhances proteome half-lives more effectively than rapamycin in old hearts (30% vs 12% increase), suggesting distinct mechanisms for age-related proteostasis that merit further mechanistic study.

reviewer_objections: The proposed sex-specific effects are based on limited mouse data from a single genetic model (Apc(1638N/+)); extrapolation to human cancers is speculative without corroborative evidence
Confounding variables such as diet composition, genetic background, or environmental factors were not controlled across studies cited, weakening causal claims
The mechanisms linking CR to sex-specific cancer suppression—e.g., through leptin or IGF-1 modulation—are not elucidated in the cited facts, relying on associative rather than interventional data
next_extractions: Extract studies on CR effects in female mice with other cancer models (e.g., breast, ovarian) to assess generalizability of sex-specific responses
Harvest data on sex hormone interactions with CR in tumorigenesis, particularly in Apc mutant models
Look for human observational studies on sex differences in dietary restriction and cancer risk, focusing on intestinal malignancies
